task.name: forge triage: operator ratification applies dispositions; punt closes require reason codes
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2229
---

## What

The decision-and-application stage of `forge triage`. The operator sees the full picture — proposals, punt reviews, flagged disagreements — and ratifies or overrides per finding. Only then does anything change: ratified dispositions are applied mechanically (milestone assignment, Hygiene pool assignment, or close-with-reason-code), and every applied outcome is recorded in the audit substrate.

This slice also lands the punt-rationale requirement #717 deferred to this epic: a punt-close always carries a reason code from the documented fixed set, cited evidence in the closing comment, and a close through this flow without a recognized code is refused.

## Why

Slice 4 of epic #1033, blocked by the punt-review slice. The epic's central invariant lives here: milestone assignment is an operator decision — agents propose targets, and nothing is applied without explicit per-finding ratification. The same boundary the escalation advisor established (the system no longer auto-rejects; the operator selects) applied to backlog dispositions.

## Acceptance criteria

- No disposition is applied without explicit per-finding operator ratification. Ratifying applies exactly the proposal the operator reviewed; overriding applies the operator's alternative instead — in both cases the applied outcome, the decision, and the evidence reference are written to the audit substrate.
- A punt application closes the issue with a reason code from the documented fixed set and a closing comment citing the evidence. A missing or unrecognized reason code is refused and the finding stays open — for operator overrides exactly as for agent proposals.
- A fix disposition applies the milestone or pool target the operator confirmed at ratification, which may differ from the proposed target.
- Application is resumable: if it halts partway (a failed API call mid-batch), re-running completes the remaining ratified dispositions without duplicating comments, labels, or closures on the ones already applied.
- A finding whose state changed between proposal and ratification (closed meanwhile, labels changed, new commits invalidating the evidence) is surfaced as stale and skipped, never blindly applied.

## Example

```
forge triage — ratification (15 findings, 2 flagged)

#1312  punt/verified-stale, review concurred    → [accept]
       closed, reason=verified-stale, evidence comment posted
#943   punt/cosmetic — CHALLENGED               → [override: fix_later → Hygiene]
       operator note: reviewer is right, reachable on resume path
#659   needs_verification                       → [accept]
       remains open, unverified state recorded
```

## Non-goals

- No headless / non-interactive operation — next slice.
- No change to the labels findings are created with.

handoff.summary: Added the operator ratification/application stage for `forge triage`: proposal runs now persist packet and stable finding-snapshot context, the audit substrate gained upserted per-finding application records plus read-model helpers, and a new interactive `--ratify` flow records accept/override/skip decisions before applying milestone or punt-close effects with stale checks and idempotency markers. The CLI now dispatches report, proposal, and ratification modes; docs were updated to describe the new behavior; focused tests cover accept, override, punt refusal, stale skip, resume/idempotency, parser/dispatch, and the no-audit refusal path. A late-suite inherited-agent zombie logging race also surfaced during validation and was fixed in `sprint/live_stories.py` so `make dev-check` passes cleanly.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] The ratification flow has two blocking acceptance-criteria gaps: punt overrides can close without cited evidence, and stale findings can be marked applied when the target milestone is already present. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Ratification/application flow is well-structured and audited, but the stale check compares two snapshot dictionaries built by different, non-equivalent producers, so real findings are falsely marked stale and nothing is applied.

findings.description: When a ratified fix finding's live milestone already matched the target, the application path recorded it as applied before running stale detection, so a label or evidence change between proposal and ratification was not surfaced as stale.
When an operator overrode a no-citation proposal to punt and accepted the blank evidence prompt, the flow could post a closing comment with no evidence rows and close the issue.

When ratifying a proposal run generated from a real backlog report, the stale check compares a digest of the stored proposal-time snapshot against a digest of the live snapshot, and the two are produced by different code paths that normalise the issue body differently (the report artifact is parsed with a strip on the body, while the live collector keeps the raw GitHub body), so any finding whose issue body has leading or trailing whitespace - the common case for tracker issues - is reported as 'live finding state diverged from the reviewed snapshot' and skipped even though nothing about the finding changed.

A proposal event recorded before this change carries neither a stored packet nor a finding snapshot, and the prompt path raises a hard error for the missing packet, aborting the entire ratification command, while the documentation states that runs predating stored snapshots are surfaced as stale and skipped.

A behavioural change to inherited-agent wait logging in the sprint subsystem is included in this branch, adding a second liveness probe and a loop restart inside the operator-facing log branch, which is unrelated to the triage ratification spec and is not covered by any test in this change.

findings.description: When a rerun sees a ratified punt whose prior attempt already posted the marker comment and closed the issue, the application path records the finding as stale instead of recognizing the already-applied close.

The application path checks live staleness before its idempotency short-circuits, and the staleness check treats any closed issue as stale, so the branch that recognises an already-closed punt carrying the idempotency marker as already applied can never execute and a punt whose close succeeded but whose durable record was never updated is reported as stale on the next run instead of applied.

The ratification documentation states that already-closed punts carrying the idempotency marker are treated as already applied on rerun, while the flow classifies any closed issue as stale before reaching that recognition, so the documented resume behaviour does not match what the command does.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (GitHub close vocabulary vs TheForge punt reason codes) is retired by the plan's mitigation — the code lives in the audit row and closing comment, gh close is only transport — but the plan does not name the transport helper. There is no shared gh-mutation module for triage; the existing precedents are per-command private helpers (cli/todo.py:221 gh issue close, cli/report.py:160 gh issue comment, coordinator/diagnose_flow.py:517 _post_comment). Note also config/defaults.py:66 documents that the *proposer* stage has no shell by design — the ratification flow is operator-driven CLI, not agent-driven, so that invariant is not violated, but the dev agent must not route application through the proposer's tool surface.
  Suggestion: Have the application flow call subprocess with an explicit argv list (no shell) from its own helper, mirroring diagnose_flow._post_comment, and keep it entirely out of the agent-invoked proposer path.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Ratification depends on proposal events existing in the audit substrate, but triage_proposal_flow._record_run is skipped when the proposal run was invoked with --no-audit (cli/triage.py passes record=not args.no_audit). --ratify against such a run will find zero events.
  Suggestion: Have the ratify path fail with an explicit message naming the triage_run_id and the --no-audit cause rather than reporting 'no findings'.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (conservative staleness on cosmetic evidence drift) is retired by the plan's fail-closed choice plus the Step 5 stale-skip test. Residual: proposal events written before Step 2 lands carry no snapshot, so ratifying an older run has nothing to compare against.
  Suggestion: Treat a missing snapshot as stale (fail closed) rather than as 'unchanged'; single-operator repo makes any migration unnecessary.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] During resume operations, checking if a comment was already posted via gh issue view or comment search requires a stable search key. Using the triage_run_id as part of the comment payload acts as a reliable idempotency marker.
- [P2] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] The 'Hygiene' milestone might not exist on the target repository at run time, which could cause gh issue edit to fail on that step.

finding_registry.description: When a ratified fix finding's live milestone already matched the target, the application path recorded it as applied before running stale detection, so a label or evidence change between proposal and ratification was not surfaced as stale.
When an operator overrode a no-citation proposal to punt and accepted the blank evidence prompt, the flow could post a closing comment with no evidence rows and close the issue.

When ratifying a proposal run generated from a real backlog report, the stale check compares a digest of the stored proposal-time snapshot against a digest of the live snapshot, and the two are produced by different code paths that normalise the issue body differently (the report artifact is parsed with a strip on the body, while the live collector keeps the raw GitHub body), so any finding whose issue body has leading or trailing whitespace - the common case for tracker issues - is reported as 'live finding state diverged from the reviewed snapshot' and skipped even though nothing about the finding changed.

A proposal event recorded before this change carries neither a stored packet nor a finding snapshot, and the prompt path raises a hard error for the missing packet, aborting the entire ratification command, while the documentation states that runs predating stored snapshots are surfaced as stale and skipped.

A behavioural change to inherited-agent wait logging in the sprint subsystem is included in this branch, adding a second liveness probe and a loop restart inside the operator-facing log branch, which is unrelated to the triage ratification spec and is not covered by any test in this change.

When a rerun sees a ratified punt whose prior attempt already posted the marker comment and closed the issue, the application path records the finding as stale instead of recognizing the already-applied close.

The application path checks live staleness before its idempotency short-circuits, and the staleness check treats any closed issue as stale, so the branch that recognises an already-closed punt carrying the idempotency marker as already applied can never execute and a punt whose close succeeded but whose durable record was never updated is reported as stale on the next run instead of applied.

The ratification documentation states that already-closed punts carrying the idempotency marker are treated as already applied on rerun, while the flow classifies any closed issue as stale before reaching that recognition, so the documented resume behaviour does not match what the command does.

When a stored proposal event carries neither a usable issue number in its snapshot nor an issue reference in the hash-number form, the application path raises out of the per-finding helper, aborting the whole ratification run partway through a batch after earlier findings have already been applied to the tracker.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
